headline: Records early, an AI scare Thursday, and a quiet rotation into defensive stocks
push: Defensives led while chips and small caps lagged.
summary: The S&P 500 gained about 1.2% and set a record close on Tuesday, but the leadership changed during the week. Utilities, consumer staples, energy and health care each rose 2.8% to 4%. Tech slipped, and small caps fell about 0.9%. The 10-year Treasury yield touched its highest level since 2002 on Wednesday before a solid bond auction pulled it back. On Thursday, a report that OpenAI's revenue was running about $20 billion below what investors had been told hit chip and AI stocks. Friday brought a broad bounce into the start of bank earnings season. The VIX stayed near 15 all week, so the moves look like a rotation rather than fear.
mood_detail: The VIX ended near 14.8, down from 15.3 the Friday before. 194 of the 276 names the dashboard tracks rose for the week, and the equal-weight S&P beat the regular S&P. That says the average stock did better than the giants this week.

headlines: Nasdaq closed at a record 27,477 (+1.05%); S&P 500 +0.66% to 7,773.95.
S&P 500 closed at a record 7,818.93 (+0.6%), its first close above 7,800; Nasdaq also closed at a record.
Cooling Treasury yields and easing oil drove the gains; Marvell +5.8%, Broadcom +3.7%, AMD +2.8%.
Constellation Energy (CEG) rose after a long-term deal to supply Google with electricity.
Stocks pulled back from records as bond yields and oil rose; the Russell 2000 fell 1.31%.
The 10-year yield hit 5.364% intraday, its highest since 2002, then eased after strong demand at a $39 billion auction.
Brent traded above $102 intraday and settled at $100.20.
Reports put OpenAI's annualized revenue near $50 billion, about $20 billion below figures given to investors; AI stocks sold off.
Nasdaq fell about 1.2%; chipmakers, up more than 80% this year, dropped 3.4% as a group (Reuters). The Dow edged up.
Oil prices and Treasury yields stabilized.
Telecoms sank after SpaceX agreed to buy an 800 MHz spectrum portfolio, a direct wireless threat: AT&T (T), Verizon (VZ) and T-Mobile (TMUS) fell 9-13%.
Humana (HUM) jumped about 11% on positive Medicare Advantage quality ratings.

themes.title: Rates near 24-year highs
themes.text: The 10-year yield touched 5.36% on Wednesday, its highest since 2002, as oil above $100 kept inflation worries alive. A strong auction calmed it, and it ended the week near 5.2%. Rate-sensitive small caps lagged.

themes.title: AI trade tested
themes.text: Thursday's OpenAI revenue report was the first real crack in this year's AI story. Chip names such as ARM, INTC, TER, SWKS and ON finished the week down 8-13%. Power producers tied to AI data centers, VST and CEG, rose about 15%.

themes.title: Defense over offense
themes.text: Utilities (+4.0%), staples (+3.6%), energy (+3.6%) and health care (+2.8%) led the sectors. Tech (-0.5%) and industrials (-0.4%) lagged.

themes.title: Telecom shock
themes.text: SpaceX's spectrum purchase knocked about 9-13% off the big three wireless carriers in a single day.

questions: Utilities and staples led while the S&P set records. Is that rotation a warning about growth, or is money just leaving crowded AI trades?
The 10-year at 5.2-5.4% competes with stocks for money. What level would make you trim, and which of your watchlist names are most rate-sensitive?
Banks report next week, with JPM, GS, WFC and C on Tuesday. What would you need to hear on loan losses and the consumer to trust this market's strength?
gaps: No daily dashboard snapshot was saved for Monday or Tuesday (the GitHub save was fixed on Tuesday), so those two days show prices and headlines only.
